ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: On October 24, 2014, the “Chang'e-5” flight test vehicle was launched from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, and successfully returned to the ground 8 days later by means of “skip reentry.” “Skip reentry” refers to a spacecraft entering the atmosphere after shutting down its engine, relying on atmospheric lift to rush out of the atmosphere again, reducing its speed and then entering the atmosphere again, as shown in the figure; the dashed line is the boundary of the atmosphere. It is known that the radius of the Earth is R, the distance from the Earth's center to point d is r, and the gravitational acceleration at the Earth's surface is g. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The speed of the flight test vehicle at point a is greater than its speed at point c

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On October 24, 2014, the “Chang'e-5” flight test vehicle was launched from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center, and successfully returned to the ground 8 days later by means of “skip reentry.” “Skip reentry” refers to a spacecraft entering the atmosphere after shutting down its engine, relying on atmospheric lift to rush out of the atmosphere again, reducing its speed and then entering the atmosphere again, as shown in the figure; the dashed line is the boundary of the atmosphere. It is known that the radius of the Earth is R, the gravitational acceleration at the Earth's surface is g. According to the process shown in the figure, what is the relative magnitude relationship between the speeds of the flight test vehicle at points a and c?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The speed of the flight test vehicle at point a is greater than its speed at point c
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle labeled “Earth,” and outside it there is a dashed circular boundary labeled “atmosphere.” The flight trajectory is a solid line; point a is near the dashed atmosphere boundary on the left side, the trajectory enters inside the dashed boundary from a, passes through b, and then reaches point c located on the dashed boundary, and rushes out of the atmosphere near c; afterward the trajectory also passes through d and e. It can be seen from the figure that both point a and point c are on the same dashed atmosphere boundary, so their distances to the Earth's center are the same. Then reason: The question stem states that the flight test vehicle enters the atmosphere after shutting down its engine, and relies on atmospheric lift to rush out of the atmosphere again and reduce its speed. In the process from a to c there is no engine supplying energy, and when moving inside the atmosphere it will be subject to air resistance; resistance does negative work, causing mechanical energy to decrease. Since a and c are on the same atmosphere boundary and their distances to the Earth's center are the same, their gravitational potential energies are the same; the decrease in mechanical energy can only be reflected as a decrease in kinetic energy. Therefore the kinetic energy at point c is less than the kinetic energy at point a, that is, the speed at point c is less than the speed at point a.
